**The proposed answer $P_X(t)=t^{14}$ is wrong: the top-degree rational homology $\widetilde H_{14}(X;\mathbb Q)$ vanishes.**

**Reduction to Borel–Moore homology.** $X=Y^+$ with $Y$ closed in $\mathbb R^{18}$, so $\widetilde H_k(X;\mathbb Q)\cong H^{BM}_k(Y;\mathbb Q)$. Let $Y_1=Y\setminus S$, which is closed in $Y$ and has dimension $13$. The long exact sequence gives
$$H^{BM}_{14}(Y_1)=0 \to H^{BM}_{14}(Y)\to H^{BM}_{14}(S)\cong\mathbb Q\xrightarrow{\ \delta\ } H^{BM}_{13}(Y_1),$$
so $H^{BM}_{14}(Y)=\ker\delta$. The class $\delta[S]$ is the boundary of the fundamental chain of $S$, and $\widetilde H_{14}(X)=0$ exactly when this boundary is nonzero.

**The boundary is nonzero.** Near a generic point of the wall $\{a=b\}$ (where the roots of multiplicity 3 and 1 merge into a root of multiplicity 4), the stratum $S$ lies on only one side. Nearby polynomials in $S$ must have the triple root to the left of the simple root, so $S$ is locally a half-space bounded by this wall. The wall is a 13-dimensional cell of $Y_1$, and $\delta[S]$ has coefficient $\pm1$ on it. The same holds for the walls $\{b=c\}$, $\{c=d\}$, and the locus where $Q$ acquires a real double root. A 13-chain in a 13-dimensional space is zero in homology only if it is zero as a chain, so $\delta[S]\neq0$, hence $H^{BM}_{14}(Y)=0$.

**Sanity check.** Take the analogous profile $(3,1)$ in monic degree 4. Then $Y=\{(x-u)^3(x-v): u\le v\}$ is a closed half-plane, so $X$ is a closed disk and $\widetilde H_*(X)=0$. The top class dies in the same way, which contradicts the pattern $t^{\dim S}$ suggested by the proposed solution.

**Flaws in the proposed argument.** The Alexander-duality step only shows the link class is nontrivial in $\mathbb R^{18}\setminus Y$. It does not account for the boundary walls, which kill the top class. The appeal to shellability and Cohen–Macaulayness of a "poset of strata" over $\mathbb Q$ is asserted without justification, and it cannot force the homology into a single degree. I have not computed the correct full polynomial $P_X(t)$, but the coefficient of $t^{14}$ is definitively $0$, not $1$.

VERDICT: REJECT
